title: Along My Earthly Way
description: Along My Earthly Way in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Edmeston wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 521 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Why sayest thou — my way is hid from the Lord?"”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-long my earth-ly way, How man-y clouds are spread! Dark-ness, with scarce one cheer-ful ray, Seems gath-ering o'er my head.

lines: Along my earthly way,
How many clouds are spread!
Darkness, with scarce one cheerful ray,
Seems gathering o'er my head.
Yet, Father, thou art love:
O hide not from my view!
But when I look, in prayer, above,
Appear in mercy through!
My pathway is not hid;
Thou knowest all my need;
And I would do as Israel did, —
Follow where thou wilt lead.
Lead me, and then my feet
Shall never, never stray;
But safely I shall reach the seat
Of happiness and day.
And O from that bright throne,
I shall look back, and see, —
The path I went, and that alone,
Was the right path for me.

licence: Public domain: James Edmeston died in 1867.
credits: Words by James Edmeston (1791–1867), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
